description: Evaluates whether the skill produces expert-level UI/UX design decisions

criteria.description: Must organize content with clear hierarchy — primary actions prominent, secondary actions subordinate
Must minimize clicks/taps to complete primary tasks (3-click rule)
Must design meaningful empty states with guidance (not blank screens)
Must use progressive disclosure — show essentials first, details on demand
Every user action must have visible feedback (loading, success, error)
Must maintain visual and interaction consistency across similar components
Must design mobile-first, then enhance for larger screens

testPrompt: Design the UX for a workout logger that a personal trainer uses during live sessions with clients. They need to: select exercises from a library, log sets/reps/weight in real time, add notes, and mark the session complete. Must work on a phone held in one hand.
